learner_operation: Identify the specified unchanged pivot row and cleared column, determine both integer cancellation coefficients from matrix entries, verify both complete row additions and select the matching pair.

fixed_features.feature: 3x3 integer matrices, one unchanged pivot row, two row additions and five radio choices.
fixed_features.justification: All ten assessed source cases and the Introduction tutorial teach this two-operation workload; changing operators or response type would change the skill.

fixed_features.feature: Four sign combinations of the principal magnitude pair plus one source-type magnitude distractor.
fixed_features.justification: Retains source bank error types. A magnitude error can be rejected mathematically, but either operation sign still depends on the matrices.

fixed_features.feature: Small CLI batches use one visible bank shape; extra signs fixed inside that shape for one batch.
fixed_features.justification: The four independent correct sign cases are exercised against the same cue, which prevents that cue predicting either sign. Across batches all three shapes and all source profiles remain available; this scheduling does not fix correct signs.

answer_roles.role: Unchanged pivot row and zeroed column
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any of the nine row-column coordinates while keeping nonzero pivot and integral coefficients.
answer_roles.observed: All nine explicit boundaries; fixed A tested with changed column and changed pivot row; prompt, answer and solution follow targets.

answer_roles.role: Signed coefficients of the first and second target rows
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Vary both signs independently, magnitudes including units, and equal magnitudes in unit-error profiles.
answer_roles.observed: All four sign pairs in the exact five-record delivered batch and each shape in 26 fresh CLI records; all ten fixed-bank quartets change the correct answer without changing bank content.

answer_roles.role: Extra distractor magnitude coordinate and sign
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Unit error in either coordinate or swapped magnitudes; independent signs subject to five distinct choices.
answer_roles.observed: All three shapes survive fresh CLI delivery. Retained author test independently rerun covers every extra sign/role in 52 identical-bank groups.
Correct displayed positions range 1–5 in eight actual UI cases; authored bank order and UI order differ.

coverage.case: Original fidelity: ten questions, twelve complete captured banks and canonical example matrices/operations
coverage.result: All mathematical banks and keyed choices match. Canonical example has no captured answer bank; no claim of bank replay there.

coverage.case: Relevant sign and target changes; irrelevant non-target change
coverage.result: Answers, matrices, explanations and native grader outcomes follow the intended dependency.

coverage.case: Actual runner batch, seed 1278010737, easy, count 5
coverage.result: All 5 survive filtering. Old opposite-outlier-first-sign shortcut succeeds 2/5, same-sign variant 3/5. All four coefficient-sign decisions survive.
26/26 survive delivery; each represented shape has all four sign pairs and counterexamples to both cue polarities.

30 direct samples collapse to 6 semantic prompts because the same three seeds were applied across profiles. The three swapped-magnitude survivors happen to share second-sign relationships. This diagnostic fixture bypasses the revised CLI batch scheduler; current emitted batches explicitly include counterexamples, so it does not demonstrate a current batch defect.

counterfactuals.change: Hold seed=472, q-42531 bank, pivot and other entries fixed; change A[1][0] from 2 to -2 and the required first coefficient from -2 to +2.
counterfactuals.expected: First operation and B must change; prior (-2,+3) pair must be rejected.
counterfactuals.observed: Same bank, different correct pair and B. Native grader accepts base pair before change and rejects it afterward. Actual UI shows changed sign and solution operation.
counterfactuals.justification: Cancellation depends on the target entry, as demonstrated by source q-42531 and tutorial.

counterfactuals.change: Hold cancellation entries, pivot and seed fixed; change A[1][1] from 5 to 6.
counterfactuals.expected: Correct row-operation pair unchanged; transformed non-target entry and intermediate matrix update.
counterfactuals.observed: (-2,+3) remains correct and native-accepted; intermediate and final row entries update from 1 to 2. Screenshot verified.
counterfactuals.justification: The ratio in the eliminated column determines the multiplier; non-target entries only change the resulting row.

counterfactuals.change: Keep A=[[1,1,3],[2,1,5],[4,3,7]] fixed; change cleared column 0 to 1, then pivot row 0 to 1.
counterfactuals.expected: Cleared column, target rows, coefficients and B follow selected target; solutions name the new pivot.
counterfactuals.observed: Coefficient pairs (-2,-4), (-1,-3) and (-1,-3) with changed target rows; all displayed banks independently evaluated, accepted/rejected by native grader, and rendered target references inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: Sources include above, below, and above-and-below elimination and all three cleared columns.

stages_examined: CLI batch sign/shape rejection and duplicate prevention
Actual publisher normalization and inventory/within-batch deduplication
Question-selection positive-weight, zero-weight, absent-weight and history-exclusion rules
delivery.result: Captured basis 5580: runner batch 5/5 and fresh CLI batches 26/26 survive. All intended sign counterexamples remain available. No stored generated question exists; original source questions are not generated-pool repair candidates. Selection preserves equal support within positive easy band; no live publication performed.

limitations: Finite audit does not exclude every imaginable shortcut.
No live learner policy/history or new database entity IDs supplied; selection is a faithful read-only model of the captured all-easy candidates, with ordering and history limits recorded.
A learner consuming only part of the finite pool is not guaranteed all four sign cases. Future inventory deduplication can alter delivered coverage.
Canonical source example has no captured answer bank; two assessed questions have duplicate selection fields, both complete banks checked.
No free-entry family is supported, so equivalent-entry notation tests are inapplicable; all radio choices and controlled response preservation/rejection were exercised.
